title: Accessibility and compactness of bounded cocone categories
statement: Use universes, filteredness, accessibility and compactness from [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and coherent diagrams and cocone categories from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\alpha<\beta$ be infinite regular cardinals in the smaller universe, with $\beta$ uncountable and $a^b<\beta$ for all cardinals $a<\beta$ and $b<\alpha$. Let $\mathcal C$ be a $\beta$-accessible infinity category. Let $K$ be an $\alpha$-small simplicial set and let $p:K\to\mathcal C$ be a coherent diagram whose vertex values are $\beta$-compact. Write $\mathcal C_{p/}$ for the infinity category of coherent cocones $p\to\Delta_K c$, with its higher compatibility simplices, and $U:\mathcal C_{p/}\to\mathcal C$ for the apex projection. Then $\mathcal C_{p/}$ is $\beta$-accessible. A cocone $q\in\mathcal C_{p/}$ is $\beta$-compact if and only if its apex $U(q)$ is $\beta$-compact in $\mathcal C$. For every small $\beta$-filtered infinity category $I$, the apex projection creates and detects colimit cocones of $I$-diagrams: a coherent cocone on a diagram $I\to\mathcal C_{p/}$ is colimiting if and only if its image under $U$ is colimiting, and every colimiting apex cocone lifts, up to a contractible space of choices, to one in $\mathcal C_{p/}$. The empty shape $K$ is allowed.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2 of prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint, compact-slice cofinality input: HTT Lemma 5.4.5.14 and Proposition 5.4.5.15 (use tau=beta and kappa=alpha there), as used in the proof of Lemma 5.4.6.1; filtered colimits are computed at the apex because filtered indexing categories are weakly contractible Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text:
Put $H=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$ and $Q=\mathcal C_{p/}$. The coherent cocone calculus makes $H,Q$ quasicategories and gives, for $q=(c,u:p\to\Delta_Kc)$ and $r=(d,v:p\to\Delta_Kd)$, the natural formula
$$\operatorname{Map}_Q(q,r)\simeq\operatorname{fib}_{v}\bigl(\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,d)\xrightarrow{a\mapsto\Delta_K(a)u}\operatorname{Map}_H(p,\Delta_Kd)\bigr).$$
Local smallness of $\mathcal C$ follows from accessibility. The local-smallness clause of the spine/tower lemma makes $H$ locally small, so this homotopy fiber is small and $Q$ is locally small. We compute with small mapping-space models using the coherent mapping bifunctor of the transport-classification node. The inclusion of small spaces into the larger space universe is fully faithful and preserves small colimits by the space-universe node. Thus all compactness comparisons below, computed with small models, are also the comparisons required by the larger-space-universe definition of compactness; no change of compactness convention is implicit.

source.place: Lemmas 5.4.5.13-15, coherent cocone model and local-smallness preliminaries; mapping-space formulation of the argument.

proof.text:
Let $I$ be any small $\beta$-filtered quasicategory, without a bound on its cardinality. The filtered weak-contractibility assertion of the coslice-colimit node shows that $I$ is weakly contractible. Consequently $I\to *$ satisfies the comma criterion (its sole comma is $I$), and the cofinal-comma node shows that restriction identifies cocones on an object of any quasicategory with cocones on its constant $I$-diagram. In particular $*\to H$ with value $p$ preserves $I$-colimits. Pointwise colimits give $I$-colimits in $H$, in $\operatorname{Arr}(H)$ and in $H\times H$; the constant-diagram functor $\Delta_K:\mathcal C\to H$ preserves them. Model $Q$ as the strict pullback of
$$\operatorname{Arr}(H)\xrightarrow{(\operatorname{ev}_0,\operatorname{ev}_1)}H\times H\xleftarrow{(p,\Delta_K)}*\times\mathcal C.$$
The endpoint restriction is an isofibration by the exponential-corner node applied to $\partial\Delta^1\subseteq\Delta^1$ and $H\to *$. The isofibration-pullback node therefore identifies this strict pullback with the categorical homotopy pullback (enlarge the ambient universe so all displayed categories are small there). Both legs preserve $I$-colimits, so the pullback-colimit node supplies colimits in $Q$ and characterizes them by their two components. For a cocone already in $Q$, its source component in $H$ is the constant identity cocone at $p$, which is colimiting by the preceding argument. Its target component is obtained by applying $\Delta_K$ to its apex cocone. Hence an apex colimit gives a colimit in $Q$. Conversely a colimit in $Q$ gives a colimit in $*\times\mathcal C$, hence an apex colimit. For a chosen colimiting apex cocone with vertex $c$, start with a colimit in $Q$ with vertex $(c_0,u_0)$. The two apex colimit cocones are initial objects of the same cocone category, so there is an equivalence between them, with apex component $e:c_0\simeq c$ and its coherent compatibility with the diagram. Postcompose $u_0$ with $\Delta_K(e)$ to obtain the new cocone $p\to\Delta_Kc$. Postcomposing the colimit cocone in $Q$ with this equivalence, and using the compatibility just specified, gives a colimit whose apex cocone is identified with the chosen one. Componentwise equivalences and the cocone calculus justify these compositions, including their higher simplices. The cores of colimit-cocone categories in $Q$ and $\mathcal C$ are nonempty contractible spaces by the coherent cocone calculus. The induced map between them is therefore an equivalence; its homotopy fiber over the chosen apex cocone is contractible. This is precisely the space of lifts, with the identification of their apex cocone included. Thus $U$ creates and detects all the colimits claimed.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.5.14 and the pointwise/pullback proof behind Lemma 5.4.5.13; Corollary 5.1.2.3 and Lemma 5.4.5.5. Creation/detection expanded by the pullback model.

proof.text:
We need the following bounded-diagram calculation, without assuming $\alpha$-accessibility of $\mathcal C$: for every $\beta$-small simplicial set $L$ and pointwise $\beta$-compact $a:L\to\mathcal C$, the object $a$ is $\beta$-compact in $\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal C)$. All the colimits tested are computed pointwise. First prove this for $L=\Delta^n$. For $n=0$ it is the definition of compactness. For an arrow $a_0\to a_1$, the arrow-morphism-square node expresses its mapping space to $b_0\to b_1$ as
$$\operatorname{Map}(a_0,b_0)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}(a_0,b_1)}\operatorname{Map}(a_1,b_1).$$
Each of the three terms preserves $\beta$-filtered colimits by compactness of $a_0,a_1$; the finite-limit case of the spaces interchange node makes the homotopy pullback preserve them. For $n>1$, replace $\Delta^n$ by its spine using the spine equivalence. Adjoin the $n$ edges successively along the shared vertices. Mapping excision gives a homotopy pullback at each attachment, so induction on the number of edges and the same finite-limit interchange prove the claim for the spine, hence for $\Delta^n$. All formulas are natural in the target diagram, so they identify the actual compactness comparison.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.4.13, proof (1)-(3): vertices, arrows and spines; Lemma 5.4.5.13.

proof.text: Continue the calculation of step 3 by induction on the dimension of a finite-dimensional $\beta$-small $L$. In dimension zero, the mapping space is the product of the mapping spaces for its fewer than $\beta$ vertices, by the degreewise internal-functor definition; apply the product case of the spaces interchange node. At dimension $n$, attach the disjoint union of its nondegenerate $n$-simplices to the $(n-1)$-skeleton along their boundaries. This is a degreewise simplicial pushout: the nondegenerate-decomposition node says every simplex is uniquely a degeneracy of a nondegenerate simplex, so the newly attached simplices meet only in their prescribed boundary faces. Mapping excision expresses the mapping space as a homotopy pullback. Its boundary terms satisfy the induction hypothesis, its simplex terms satisfy step 3, and the disjoint unions give products of fewer than $\beta$ factors. The spaces interchange node applies to these products and the homotopy pullback. For general $L$, use $L=\bigcup_{n\geq0}\operatorname{sk}_n L$ and the spine/tower node's natural mapping-space limit formula. Because $\beta$ is uncountable, the nerve of $\mathbb N^{\mathrm{op}}$ is $\beta$-small, and its limit commutes with $\beta$-filtered colimits by the spaces interchange node. This completes the calculation, including $L=\varnothing$: its mapping space is terminal, and the empty-limit case of the same interchange theorem applies. The argument uses $L$-smallness at rank $\beta$, not at rank $\alpha$. Since $\alpha<\beta$, the given $K$ is $\beta$-small.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.4.13, proof (4)-(6), cellular attachment and inverse tower; Lemma 5.4.5.13.

proof.text:
Let $q=(c,u)$ have $\beta$-compact apex. By steps 3-4 the boundary diagram $p$ is $\beta$-compact in $H$. In the mapping-space fiber formula of step 1, both functors of $r$,
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,U(r)),\qquad \operatorname{Map}_H(p,\Delta_K U(r)),$$
preserve $\beta$-filtered colimits, by step 2, pointwise colimits for $\Delta_K$, and the two compactness assertions. The point selecting $v$ is a coherent natural transformation from the terminal-space functor to the second functor. Thus the fiber formula is a finite limit of the displayed two functors and the terminal-space functor. The spaces interchange node makes this finite limit preserve $\beta$-filtered colimits, including the colimit of the constant terminal space. It follows that $\operatorname{Map}_Q(q,-)$ preserves them. This proves that every compact-apex cocone is $\beta$-compact.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.5.13, compactness under the fixed-boundary homotopy-fiber formula.

proof.text: Let $D\subseteq\mathcal C$ be the replete full subcategory of $\beta$-compact objects and $Q_D\subseteq Q$ the full subcategory of cocones whose apex lies in $D$. Since $D$ is full, $Q_D$ is exactly the coherent cocone category $D_{p/}$: fullness identifies all its transformations, their compatibility homotopies and their higher simplices with those in $\mathcal C$, and every vertex of $p$ lies in $D$. $Q_D$ is replete in $Q$, because $U$ carries equivalences to equivalences and $D$ is replete. Essential smallness. By the compact-slice-density node, $D$ is equivalent to a small quasicategory $D_0$; the images of the vertices of $D_0$ form a small family $(d_j)_{j\in J}$ in $D$ such that every object of $D$ is equivalent to some $d_j$. By step 1, $H$ and $Q$ are locally small, so each set $\pi_0\operatorname{Map}_H(p,\Delta_Kd_j)$ is small; choose representatives $u_{j,s}$, $s\in S_j$, of its components and put $x_{j,s}=(d_j,u_{j,s})\in Q_D$. This is a small family. Let $q=(c,u)\in Q_D$. Choose an equivalence $e:c\to d_j$ and then $s\in S_j$ and a path $\gamma$ in $\operatorname{Map}_H(p,\Delta_Kd_j)$ from $\Delta_K(e)u$ to $u_{j,s}$. By the dual cocone fiber formula of the cone-calculus node (step 1), $(e,\gamma)$ is a point $\phi\in\operatorname{Map}_Q(q,x_{j,s})$ lying over $e$. For every $r=(d,v)\in Q$, precomposition with $\phi$ is the map of homotopy fibers over $v$ induced by the square whose top is precomposition with $e$, $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(d_j,d)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,d)$, whose bottom is the identity of $\operatorname{Map}_H(p,\Delta_Kd)$, and which commutes up to the homotopy $\Delta_K(a)\gamma$ between $a\mapsto\Delta_K(ae)u$ and $a\mapsto\Delta_K(a)u_{j,s}$. The top map is an equivalence because $e$ is one, so the induced map of homotopy fibers over the same point $v$ is an equivalence (the path-space model of the homotopy fiber in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] is invariant under an equivalence of total spaces over a fixed base). Thus precomposition with $\phi$ gives equivalences $\operatorname{Map}_Q(x_{j,s},r)\to\operatorname{Map}_Q(q,r)$, naturally in $r$. By full faithfulness of the Yoneda functor of the Yoneda node, applied to $Q^{\mathrm{op}}$ in a universe in which $Q$ is small, and the vertexwise criterion for equivalences of coherent transformations in the cone-calculus node, $\phi$ is an equivalence in $Q$. Hence $Q_D$ is the full subcategory of the locally small quasicategory $Q$ on all objects equivalent to a member of the small family $(x_{j,s})$, and the small-full-subcategory node shows that $Q_D$ is essentially small. No claim about the size of an unrestricted large slice is used. Step 5 says all objects of $Q_D$ are $\beta$-compact.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.5.15, first paragraph: essential smallness of the compact-apex full subcategory, via a small family of representatives (HTT Proposition 5.4.1.7).

proof.text: Fix $q=(c,u)\in Q$. The compact-slice-density node gives an essentially small $\beta$-filtered category $E=D_{/c}$ with its canonical source cocone colimiting at $c$. The boundary $u$ is a diagram $\widetilde p:K\to E$, because every $p(v)$ is compact. Replace $E$ by a small equivalent model and transport this diagram; filteredness and the stated colimit cocone are invariant under the equivalence by transporting cocones along a quasi-inverse and using the mapping-space colimit criterion. Put $T=E_{\widetilde p/}$ and let $V:T\to E$ be its apex projection. It is small by the explicit cocone pullback construction, and is $\beta$-filtered by the filtered-cocone clause of the cofinal-coslice node, since $K$ is $\beta$-small. For $e\in E$, an object of $(e\downarrow V)$ is a cocone from $\widetilde p$ to $t$ together with an arrow $e\to t$. Compute this comma using the arrow model: the endpoint restriction in $E$ is an isofibration, and so is its pullback with source fixed at $e$. The isofibration-pullback node therefore says that the strict pullback of this arrow category along $V$ computes the categorical homotopy comma. This model identifies the entire coherent comma category with $E_{(\widetilde p\amalg e)/}$, where the boundary has shape $K\amalg\Delta^0$: both descriptions consist of those transformations, their triangles, and their higher simplices, and restriction to the two summands gives inverse descriptions in each simplicial degree. That boundary is $\beta$-small. Hence its cocone category is $\beta$-filtered by the same cofinal-coslice node, and weakly contractible by the filtered weak-contractibility clause of the coslice-colimit node. Apply the cofinal-comma criterion to the small categories $T,E$. Restriction along $V$ preserves the canonical colimit cocone $E\to\mathcal C$ with apex $c$. Each object of $T$ gives a cocone under $p$ with compact apex together with an arrow to $q$: its arrows to $c$ and all boundary compatibilities come from its definition as a cocone inside $D_{/c}$. These assemble to a diagram $T\to Q_D$ and cocone to $q$. Its apex cocone is the just-proved colimit $c$, so step 2 makes it a colimit in $Q$. We have presented every $q$ as a small $\beta$-filtered colimit of objects of $Q_D$.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.5.15, second paragraph: the category E and its cocones; finality of the apex projection proved by its comma categories, as in Lemmas 5.3.1.21 and 5.4.5.12.

proof.text: Steps 1-2 give local smallness and all small $\beta$-filtered colimits in $Q$; steps 5-7 give an essentially small full subcategory of compact objects generating it under these colimits. These are exactly the clauses of $\beta$-accessibility. To prove the converse compactness assertion, let $q\in Q$ be $\beta$-compact and apply compact-stage factorization to its presentation of step 7 and $1_q$. There is a stage $t\in T$ and maps $q\to q_t\to q$ whose composite is homotopic to $1_q$. Applying $U$ makes $U(q)$ a homotopy retract of the compact object $U(q_t)$. Compactness is closed under such retracts directly: precomposition with the two retract maps makes $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(U(q),-)$ a retract of $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(U(q_t),-)$, compatibly with every compactness comparison. The former comparison is therefore a retract of an equivalence; composing the retraction and section with the inverse comparison gives its inverse up to the two unit homotopies. Thus $U(q)$ is compact. Together with step 5 this is the equivalence claimed. If $K$ is empty, $H$ is terminal and $Q\simeq\mathcal C$; the construction above has $\widetilde p$ empty and $T\simeq E$, so every step still applies. If $\mathcal C$ is empty, a boundary diagram can exist only for empty $K$; $Q$ is then empty, with empty compact generating subcategory, and the assertions hold vacuously. No smaller-rank accessibility is assumed or used. The sharp-cardinal hypothesis is compatible with the source but is stronger than this proof needs.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.5.15, conclusion via the compact-retract argument of Lemma 5.4.2.4 instead of the equivalent Ind-completion characterization.
